newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1- dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1- dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower following ample marketings on Tuesday, livestock dealers said.
"We have plenty of hogs and if the run is heavy again tomorrow, we could be more than $1.00 lower," an Indiana livestock dealer said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to Indiana plants were seen in range of $57.50 to $57.75, sources there said. Top prices Tuesday in Indiana/Ohio trade were reported at $58.75 by USDA.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices at the plant were seen off $0.50 at $58.00.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant were seen steady to $0.50 lower and could range $58.00 to $58.50, sources there said. Ohio hog prices were seen steady, with a top of $58.00.
Marketings on Tuesday expanded following light receipts on Monday when several packing plants were closed for plant holidays, the dealers said.

USDA said interior Iowa/southern Minnesota actual receipts on Monday were 74,000 head, well below the agency's estimate of 90,000. By comparison, receipts there on Tuesday were estimated at 110,000 head versus 106,000 a week ago and 99,000 a year ago.
